newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania, Latvia in row over reported insult.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania, Latvia in row over reported insult.

text.p: The two small Baltic states of Lithuania and Latvia locked horns on Tuesday after Latvia's prime minister was reported to have insulted the Lithuanian president's office.
The row is part of a long-running sea border dispute between the two neighbours, which quit the former Soviet Union in 1991.

Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele was quoted by the Lithuanian newspaper Verslo Zinios as saying Vilnius was being stubborn over the border issue and castigated officials from the office of Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas.
"It is not possible to agree with Brazauskas's people," the paper quoted Shkele as saying, although the Latvian foreign ministry denied Shkele made such comments.
The Lithuanian news agency ELTA said Brazauskas was angered by the remarks,
"I think an official of such rank cannot make statements of this kind," he was quoted by ELTA as telling journalists. "He does not have the right to speak like that."
The sea border between the two countries remains unsettled and Lithuania was infuriated by a 1995 agreement between Latvia and oil company Amoco for oil exploration in the disputed area.
